industry.demand: Q1FY27 (call, 23-Jul-2026): demand healthy in all markets; India strongest (PV, CV and e-2W had their best quarters in Q4FY26; India 51% of Sona's FY26 revenue); Europe growing and electrifying (BEV, strong and plug-in hybrids); US EV sales weak (-16% in FY26, -28% YoY in Q4FY26) with a shift to hybrids; China mixed. OEMs are constrained by supply chains, not demand, in EVs.
industry.costs: Steel, aluminium, copper, freight, packaging and energy inflation since late 2025; pass-through to OEMs lags 1-2 quarters; Haryana minimum-wage rise from 1-Apr-2026; new labour codes from 21-Nov-2025 (one-off Rs30 cr provision).
industry.rareEarths: China's heavy rare-earth magnet export curbs (from Apr-2025) remain; Sona has moved to light rare-earth alternatives and says it has no magnet shortage (Q1FY27 call).
industry.rail: Indian Railways capex ~Rs2.9 lakh cr; brakes, couplers and suspension are safety-critical with long approval cycles; new HVAC (Rs2,000-2,500 cr market) and electric panels (~Rs1,500 cr) approvals in Q4FY26 (Q4FY26 call).
industry.evShare: BEV share of Sona's automotive product revenue: 2% FY20, 25% FY22, 36% FY25, 35% FY26, 44% Q1FY27.
industry.src: q1call pp.7-9; q4call pp.2-4, 13-15; ar26 MD&A pp.64-75

strengths: Engineering and frugal design: 19 products conceived and scaled in-house in seven years (Rs1,800 cr annualised revenue); R&D Rs126 cr in FY26 (2.8% of revenue)
Global scale in a niche: 8.7% of world differential gears, 4.2% of starter motors; 55-90% of India's differential gears
Early EV positioning: 69 EV programmes, 36 customers; differential assemblies for e-axles worldwide
DENSO chose Sona as a partner and will pay royalties for its 2W/3W technology
Net cash; ROCE ~16% (company basis) even after the QIP
weaknesses: Customers are huge OEMs that set prices; content is component-level, re-bid every programme
Concentration: an anchor US EV customer's model weakness cut FY26 BEV revenue; customer shares not disclosed
New lines (traction motors, railway) earn lower margins; traction motors are an assembled product with low value addition
No product-level disclosure, so investors cannot check the profitability of each line
moat.verdict: A real but narrow moat: process know-how, cost and qualification lock-in on long programmes. It earns ~24% EBITDA margins and ~16% ROCE, good but not exceptional, and the share price discounts far more.

critiques: The order book (Rs24,000 cr, 5.4x revenue) is a 10-year, management-discounted estimate; FY26 consumed Rs6,200 cr including a write-down of programmes with low ramp-up visibility.
FY26 organic revenue was roughly flat (our estimate): growth came from buying the railway business.
Margins have stepped down from 27.4% (FY25) to 24.7% (FY26) and 23.1% (Q1FY27): the band was cut twice (25-27% at IPO, 24-26%, now 23-25%).
Robotics and physical AI (Rs800 cr order book) is a narrative the market is paying for years before revenue; management itself says it is irrelevant for horizons under three years.
The DENSO deal values the 2W/3W EV business at Rs1,750 cr, 4.5x its FY26 turnover of Rs385.5 cr, well below the ~11x EV/sales the market pays for Sona as a whole.

conflicts: Revenue basis: company revenue includes net forex gain (FY26 Rs4,475 cr; Q1FY27 Rs1,310 cr) while Screener's excludes it (Rs4,449 cr; Rs1,301 cr). We model on Screener's basis.
Net Profit: Screener's consolidated row (FY26 Rs629 cr) is before the minorities' share of NOVELIC losses; attributable profit is Rs640 cr (company Rs641 cr). We use attributable (SONACOMS.patch.js).
Net cash: company Rs1,026 cr at Mar-26 (debt Rs243 cr) vs Rs837 cr in our model, which also deducts ~Rs199 cr of lease liabilities in Screener's borrowings.
QIP timing: the AR FY25 board report and the Q4FY26 call put it in Sep-2024 (some press says Jun-2024); we use Sep-2024.
